calculators.name: CHA2DS2-VASc Score
calculators.fullName: Congestive heart failure, Hypertension, Age >= 75 (doubled), Diabetes, Stroke/TIA/TE (doubled), Vascular disease, Age 65-74, Sex category
calculators.purpose: Estimates annual stroke risk in patients with non-valvular atrial fibrillation

components.name: Congestive Heart Failure
components.criteria: History of CHF or LV ejection fraction <= 40%

components.name: Hypertension
components.criteria: Resting BP > 140/90 or on antihypertensive therapy

components.name: Diabetes Mellitus
components.criteria: Fasting glucose >= 126 mg/dL or on hypoglycemic treatment

components.name: Stroke/TIA/Thromboembolism
components.criteria: Prior stroke, TIA, or systemic embolism

components.name: Vascular Disease
components.criteria: Prior MI, PAD, or aortic plaque

interpretation.recommendation: No anticoagulation (may consider aspirin in some guidelines)
Consider oral anticoagulation or aspirin (males); anticoagulation recommended (females if score driven by sex alone)
Oral anticoagulation recommended (DOAC preferred over warfarin per 2019 AHA/ACC/HRS)
Oral anticoagulation recommended
Oral anticoagulation strongly recommended
Oral anticoagulation strongly recommended; consider LAA closure if contraindicated

calculators.guidelineSource: 2019 AHA/ACC/HRS Focused Update on Atrial Fibrillation; 2020 ESC Guidelines for AF

calculators.name: HEART Score
calculators.fullName: History, ECG, Age, Risk Factors, Troponin
calculators.purpose: Predicts 6-week risk of major adverse cardiac events (MACE) in patients presenting with chest pain

options.criteria: Moderately suspicious (contains some traditional ACS features)
Highly suspicious (classic ACS presentation: substernal, exertional, radiation, diaphoresis)
Non-specific repolarization disturbance (LBBB, LVH, digoxin, pacemaker)
Significant ST deviation (ST depression or elevation not due to LBBB/LVH)
1-2 risk factors (HTN, hypercholesterolemia, DM, obesity BMI>30, smoking, family hx)
>=3 risk factors or history of atherosclerotic disease (prior MI, PCI/CABG, CVA/TIA, PAD)

interpretation.recommendation: Consider early discharge, outpatient follow-up, no further cardiac workup in ED
Admit for observation, serial troponins, consider non-invasive testing (stress test or CCTA)
Invasive strategy recommended, early cardiology consultation, consider coronary angiography

calculators.guidelineSource: Backus BE et al. (2010, 2013); 2021 AHA/ACC Chest Pain Guideline

calculators.name: Wells Score for DVT
calculators.fullName: Wells Clinical Prediction Rule for Deep Vein Thrombosis
calculators.purpose: Estimates pre-test probability of deep vein thrombosis

components.name: Active cancer (treatment within 6 months or palliative)
Paralysis, paresis, or recent plaster immobilization of the lower extremity
Recently bedridden > 3 days or major surgery within 12 weeks
Localized tenderness along the distribution of the deep venous system
Calf swelling >= 3 cm compared to asymptomatic leg (measured 10 cm below tibial tuberosity)
Pitting edema confined to the symptomatic leg
Alternative diagnosis at least as likely as DVT

interpretation.recommendation: D-dimer testing; if negative, DVT excluded. If positive, obtain compression ultrasound.
D-dimer testing; if negative, DVT excluded. If positive, obtain compression ultrasound.
Compression ultrasound recommended (skip D-dimer). If negative, consider repeat US in 5-7 days or venography.

calculators.guidelineSource: Wells PS et al. (2003); ACCP Guidelines on VTE (2016)

calculators.name: Wells Score for PE
calculators.fullName: Wells Clinical Prediction Rule for Pulmonary Embolism
calculators.purpose: Estimates pre-test probability of pulmonary embolism

components.name: Clinical signs and symptoms of DVT (leg swelling, pain with palpation of deep veins)
PE is #1 diagnosis or equally likely
Immobilization (>= 3 days) or surgery in previous 4 weeks

interpretation.recommendation: D-dimer (PERC rule may apply if all 8 criteria met); if negative, PE excluded.
D-dimer testing; if positive, CT pulmonary angiography (CTPA).
CT pulmonary angiography recommended (skip D-dimer). If CTPA unavailable, consider V/Q scan.

calculators.guidelineSource: Wells PS et al. (2000, 2001); ACCP Guidelines on VTE (2016); ESC 2019 Guidelines on PE

calculators.name: ASCVD 10-Year Risk Score
calculators.fullName: Atherosclerotic Cardiovascular Disease Pooled Cohort Equations
calculators.purpose: Estimates 10-year risk of a first atherosclerotic cardiovascular event (MI or stroke) in adults aged 40-79
calculators.formula: Pooled Cohort Equations (Goff et al., 2014). Sex- and race-specific Cox proportional hazards model using ln-transformed values of age, total cholesterol, HDL-C, treated/untreated SBP, diabetes, and smoking status.

interpretation.recommendation: Emphasize lifestyle measures. Statin therapy generally not recommended unless other risk enhancers present.

Risk discussion. Consider statin if risk-enhancing factors present (family hx, LDL >= 160, metabolic syndrome, CKD, inflammatory conditions, South Asian ancestry, elevated Lp(a), hsCRP >= 2, ABI < 0.9, CAC > 0).
Risk discussion. Moderate-intensity statin reasonable. Consider CAC score to refine if decision is uncertain (CAC = 0 favors deferral; CAC >= 100 or >= 75th percentile favors statin).
High-intensity statin recommended. Maximize lifestyle interventions. Consider adding ezetimibe or PCSK9 inhibitor if LDL remains >= 70 mg/dL.

calculators.guidelineSource: 2019 ACC/AHA Guideline on Primary Prevention of Cardiovascular Disease; 2018 AHA/ACC Cholesterol Guideline

calculators.name: CKD-EPI eGFR
calculators.fullName: Chronic Kidney Disease Epidemiology Collaboration Equation (2021)
calculators.purpose: Estimates glomerular filtration rate from serum creatinine, age, and sex (race-free 2021 equation)
calculators.formula: 2021 CKD-EPI equation (race-free): eGFR = 142 * min(SCr/kappa, 1)^alpha * max(SCr/kappa, 1)^-1.200 * 0.9938^age * (1.012 if female). Where kappa = 0.7 (female) or 0.9 (male); alpha = -0.241 (female) or -0.302 (male).

interpretation.recommendation: Monitor annually if risk factors present. Address modifiable risk factors (diabetes, hypertension).
Monitor annually. Optimize blood pressure control. Assess for albuminuria.
Referral to nephrology if progressive. Monitor every 6 months. Dose-adjust renally cleared medications.
Nephrology referral. Monitor every 3-6 months. Avoid nephrotoxins. Check PTH, vitamin D, phosphorus.
Nephrology co-management. Prepare for renal replacement therapy. Monitor monthly to every 3 months.
Dialysis or transplant planning. Urgent nephrology if not already established.

calculators.guidelineSource: Inker LA et al. NEJM 2021; KDIGO 2024 Clinical Practice Guideline for CKD
